A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MED-PE research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the relocated finite-arm lower-bound proof.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs throughout, including Appendices A–C. Table 1 and Figures 1–2 compare analytical bounds rather than original experimental outcomes.

after.justification: v2 adds original synthetic linear-bandit experiments in Appendix D. Figure 3 reports MED-PE and CRTM results across six dimensions, aggregated over 10 independent repetitions.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same experimental design, robust estimation, parameter fitting, and elimination steps. However, Corollaries 2–3 change the prescribed regularization from gamma=T^(-2epsilon/(1+epsilon)) to gamma=T^(-1), a limited retuning of the method for simplex and lp-ball action sets.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds one synthetic evaluation setting with signed coordinate arms, a normalized uniform parameter vector, and centered Pareto-II noise. v1 studies related action geometries theoretically but contains no actual empirical evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 introduces one empirically evaluated comparator: Confidence Region with Truncated Mean (CRTM), attributed to Xue et al. (2023), against MED-PE in Figure 3. v1 cites that work but does not run this comparison.

E3.justification: The new experiment specifies T=100,000, N=2d arms, dimensions 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, and 320, theta*=1/sqrt(d) times the all-ones vector, centered Pareto-II noise with alpha=2 and scale=1, and MED-PE input epsilon=0.5. Evaluation uses cumulative pseudo-regret; there is no earlier experimental protocol being revised.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a limited dimensionality sensitivity study: Figure 3 tests whether MED-PE's regret grows more slowly with ambient dimension than CRTM's. Neither version contains component ablations or broader noise-sensitivity and robustness studies.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 10 independent repetitions with identical arm sets and independent noise, and Figure 3 displays mean results with error bars. The error bars are not identified as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals, and numerical seeds are unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds one six-dimension results comparison. Appendix D reports comparable or lower MED-PE mean regret for d>=40 and a widening advantage; Figure 3 shows approximately 45,000 for MED-PE versus 60,000 for CRTM at d=320. These are newly reported outcomes, not performance changes relative to experiments in v1.

T1.justification: Corollaries 2–3 revise their regularization choices and add sqrt(dT) and d*sqrt(T), respectively, to the previous regret expressions. Appendix B changes the zero-reward probability's subtraction from 3*sqrt(d)*Delta to 2*sqrt(d)*Delta, correcting normalization. The principal minimax and kernel bounds remain unchanged; Appendix E retains the earlier finite-arm proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the principal contributions: improved minimax upper and lower bounds, geometry-dependent guarantees, and sublinear Matérn-kernel regret. The new experiment is not promoted to a new central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an interpretation of the estimator as robustified single-sample regularized least squares and explains the bias-related design penalty. Appendix D interprets the new dimension trends as consistent with Theorem 3 while explicitly limiting the experiment to a proof of concept.

D1.justification: v2 adds synthetic-data generation details and the experimental epsilon setting. It also discusses computing the truncated mean, obtaining the parameter estimate through linear optimization, and computational costs. Code, solver choices, and complete comparator tuning instructions are not supplied.

R1.justification: The application-motivation references change: v2 substitutes a different Choi et al. (2020) advertising paper, removes Jebarajakirthy et al. (2021), and replaces Baccelli et al. (2002) with Liebeherr et al. (2012). The core positioning within heavy-tailed bandit research remains stable.

P1.justification: The full Theorem 2 proof moves from Section 2.2 to Appendix E, with a shorter sketch retained in the main text. v2 expands the estimator explanation, adds a computational-complexity paragraph, lightly edits the abstract and conclusion, and switches citation notation. Most existing prose and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference typography, a redesigned title block, and substantially denser page and algorithm layouts. Table 1 gains Matérn and own-method MAB rows summarizing already discussed bounds, plus theorem pointers. Figure 1 is relocated and Figure 3 adds an empirical error-bar plot; the original analytical plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and the Appendix B probability correction improve the paper, but the added empirical evidence is internally inconsistent. Appendix D's stated arms and parameter imply pseudo-regret at most 2T/sqrt(d), approximately 11,180 at d=320 and T=100,000; Figure 3 instead shows roughly 45,000 and 60,000. The PDFs do not resolve whether the experimental description or plotted quantity is wrong. This uncertainty prevents a reliable net assessment of the theoretical and presentation benefits against the unreliable new validation.
